article:
Memory is a decision

A static page remembers nothing. Refresh, and the world is new. That is a feature for a lesson. It is a bug for an order book. A database is how the product keeps users, orders, marks on a tape, the last thing that happened.

You do not start with one. You start with a file. This site’s tape is a JSON file in GitHub. Comments are files too. That is a database for people who are not ready to operate a database. When it hurts — two writers at once, real accounts, money — you graduate.

The options you will hear

A JSON file. A SQLite file. Postgres, often through Supabase or Neon, often one click from Vercel. The branded ones wrap the same idea: tables of rows, asked for with a question.

Supabase is a fine default when you need logins and rows and you do not want to run a box. It is not mandatory for a brochure. Do not add it because a template did.

How I actually do it

Send Reorder will need real memory — shops, locations, the usual order. Meeting Mode will need dated notes. Billboard, when it wakes, will need a price that only goes up. Until that pain is real I will keep files. Files you can read beat a dashboard you do not understand.

Where noobs get stuck

A full user table for a site with no users. Or the opposite: stuffing images into the database. Or never writing the question they want to ask — “show me last week’s orders” — before they pick a vendor.

Film this

Open timeline.json. Add a row by hand. Reload the tape. Say: this is a database. Then say when it would stop being enough.

Do this before chapter 10

  • List three facts your product must remember tomorrow.
  • If the list is empty, do not add a database.
  • If the list is three lines, try a JSON file first.
  • If the list includes “money” or “other people’s accounts,” you are close to a real table.

Next: files and media — pictures do not belong in the database or in git.
